name: orlan
author: invented board game (lateral direction)
description:
INVENTED BOARD GAME ("no-name game"). Clue: a small position (5x5..6x6) drawn with
'.' empty, 'o' your pieces, 'x' enemy pieces, '#' immovable blocks. Answer: one move
"r,c>r,c" (0-indexed row,col; the scorer accepts any 4 integers in order).

HIDDEN RULES. (1) STEP LENGTH: a piece's step n is the number of its four orthogonal
neighbours that are NOT empty, counting '#' blocks AND the board rim (off-board reads as a
wall). A piece with n = 0 cannot move at all. (2) MOVE: it leaps exactly n squares in one
of the four orthogonal directions, jumping over whatever lies between; the landing square
must be on the board and empty. (3) LEGALITY: you move an 'o'. (4) GOAL: after your move
no 'x' may have a legal move under the very same rule (every 'x' is either isolated -
step 0 - or all four of its landing squares are off-board or occupied).

The three ways to win are all in the generated set: walk away so the enemy loses its only
neighbour (step -> 0); step next to an enemy so its step length changes to one whose
landing squares are all blocked; land exactly on the one square the enemy would have
leapt to. Which one applies is not visible in the picture, so a demo shows a move whose
purpose has to be reconstructed - the intended discovery path is: demo 1 gives the answer
format; demos 2-4 give (position, move) pairs from which the step-length law can be fitted
offline (distance is 1..4 and never matches piece identity, only neighbour count); the
goal is then the only simple predicate that makes the demonstrated move the unique winner
among the legal ones.

GENERATION is reverse: build a random position in which no 'x' can move (walls are added
to repair mobile ones), then un-move one 'o' by n squares where n is exactly its
neighbour count in the resulting position. Every clue is then verified by enumeration:
>= 8 legal 'o' moves, EXACTLY ONE of which achieves the goal, and at least one 'x'
currently mobile.

WITNESS LEAKS CLOSED. A constant/degenerate answer cannot work (the winner's source and
target are spread over the board and the winning distance varies 1..4). Knowing only the
movement law and guessing uniformly scores ~11%. Cheap heuristics measured over 800 seeds
score at most ~19% ("land next to an enemy"); the generator rejects any position where the
winner is the unique longest move, the unique move landing closest to an enemy, the only
move landing beside an enemy, or the only move whose mover touches an enemy - so no
heuristic gets the answer for free. Wrong but plausible movement laws (rim does not count,
8-neighbourhood, count only enemies, ignore blocks) score 4-14%, i.e. at or below the
guessing baseline, so partial credit cannot be mistaken for a correct law.
